Graduate Software Engineer — Hong Kong

Join a small product team building reliable services for university learning tools.
Responsibilities: implement Python REST APIs, design SQL queries, write automated tests,
investigate performance issues, review pull requests, and explain technical decisions to teammates.
Requirements: practical Python or TypeScript experience, knowledge of databases and testing,
clear communication, teamwork, and willingness to learn from feedback.
A strong interview example should describe your personal contribution, the technical tradeoff,
and a measured or otherwise observable result. Professional experience is not required.
This is a fictional, locally authored demonstration job description.

O*NET® 31.0 — Software Developers (15-1252.00)
Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA). https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html

These US occupational descriptions provide practice context; they are not employer requirements or a Hong Kong hiring standard.

Research, design, and develop computer and network software or specialized utility programs. Analyze user needs and develop software solutions, applying principles and techniques of computer science, engineering, and mathematical analysis. Update software or enhance existing software capabilities. May work with computer hardware engineers to integrate hardware and software systems, and develop specifications and performance requirements. May maintain databases within an application area, working individually or coordinating database development as part of a team.

Task Statements:
Task 21662: Analyze user needs and software requirements to determine feasibility of design within time and cost constraints.
Task 21669: Develop or direct software system testing or validation procedures, programming, or documentation.
Task 21664: Confer with systems analysts, engineers, programmers and others to design systems and to obtain information on project limitations and capabilities, performance requirements and interfaces.
Task 21670: Modify existing software to correct errors, adapt it to new hardware, or upgrade interfaces and improve performance.
Task 21673: Prepare reports or correspondence concerning project specifications, activities, or status.
Task 21661: Analyze information to determine, recommend, and plan installation of a new system or modification of an existing system.

Essential Skills:
Critical Thinking (2.A.2.a): Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems. Importance 3.88 on the O*NET IM scale; source date 08/2025.
Reading Comprehension (2.A.1.a): Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents. Importance 3.50 on the O*NET IM scale; source date 08/2025.
Active Learning (2.A.2.b): Understanding the implications of new information for

O*NET® 31.0 — Data Scientists (15-2051.00)
Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA). https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html
License: CC BY 4.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . VoxPrep HK selected and reformatted these rows. USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications.
These US occupational descriptions provide practice context; they are not employer requirements or a Hong Kong hiring standard.

Develop and implement a set of techniques or analytics applications to transform raw data into meaningful information using data-oriented programming languages and visualization software. Apply data mining, data modeling, natural language processing, and machine learning to extract and analyze information from large structured and unstructured datasets. Visualize, interpret, and report data findings. May create dynamic data reports.

Task Statements:
Task 21823: Analyze, manipulate, or process large sets of data using statistical software.
Task 21828: Create graphs, charts, or other visualizations to convey the results of data analysis using specialized software.
Task 21837: Test, validate, and reformulate models to ensure accurate prediction of outcomes of interest.
Task 21829: Deliver oral or written presentations of the results of mathematical modeling and data analysis to management or other end users.
Task 21836: Recommend data-driven solutions to key stakeholders.
Task 21831: Identify business problems or management objectives that can be addressed through data analysis.

Essential Skills:
Mathematics (2.A.1.e): Using mathematics to solve problems. Importance 4.38 on the O*NET IM scale; source date 08/2026.
Critical Thinking (2.A.2.a): Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems. Importance 4.25 on the O*NET IM scale; source date 08/2026.
Reading Comprehension (2.A.1.a): Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents. Importance 3.88 on the O*NET IM scale; source date 08/2026.
Speaking (2.A.1.d): Talking to others to convey information effectively. Importance 3.
